hypothesis: The wave-6 idle dimensions have floors that pre-date the recent hillclimb merges (the abort-poll park #2880, worker onecopy #2890, supervisor heap return #2899, zero-copy relay #2935, settled-child kernel release #2983, the compacting gate #3021, the refine clone cut #3013, the kitty-probe #3010 at the measured tip): the composite idle floor was UNMEASURED. (1) idle CPU + wake rate: the prior floor (worker 2.0/s, TUI ~183/s, tree 0.36% of one core) was measured at the pre-merge era with a leader-thread-only instrument. (2) idle memory: the worker-RSS, daemon-RSS and settled-child floors were measured per-lane at different heads, never as a composite. (3) launch-to-ready: cold/warm TUI and daemon-boot floors existed at b5bf28f1d (the cmp5 corpus) but not at the lane tip. (4) the TS daemon idle-eviction tier (idleEvictionMinutes: per-child passivation + whole-worker eviction) is absent from the Rust port - the setting parses but has NO consumer - so N long-idle settled children hold N x child-worker RSS indefinitely. The census re-baselines all four at the tip, scores each against the operator poles (idle CPU <1% of one core with single-digit wakes/s tree-wide; a 10MiB session settled ~200MB or better) and the best-in-class margin (reach guideline: a comfortable lead over the best reference figure), and surfaces the next candidates with measured bounds. Poles are markers, not targets; honest negatives are valid outcomes.
approach: MEASUREMENT ONLY, no product change (characterization-first decompose; the record is the deliverable). Measured tip 50e011b78 (origin/rust, the 45th hillclimb merge in; the tip moved to 78f257bf0 (#2741) DURING the census - these legs are the PRE-MOVE baseline, disclosed), fresh VM z921x7dc78inrg9s4w26gjh8 (16c/32GB, ubuntu:22.04, rustup 1.98.1, AMD EPYC 9255 - NOT pool-0 per the pool hazard), cargo build --release --locked --workspace (binary d32ed257c3197965112e431560210b80eb6c1ca096079204c950fa55d177da33, 223998912 bytes), TS reference = official 0.9.6 (69e5bb9173d0ed6df270aa59bb9919a05a2dc7076af6f830254820735bc996fb; the idle-eviction tier confirmed present in the release bundle: worker_passivate_idle_children / runIdleEvictionSweep / 'Passivated idle child' / 'Evicted idle worker' strings present; the sweep arms at supervisor startup, cadence max(60s, idle/3), verified in TS main cd1f215 source). LEGS (same-VM sequential, probe_v09 preflights pre/mid/post, noop-control pre/post, per-phase versions.json provenance, binary sha asserts per block): L1 daemon.boot (spawn->accept->hello->first_create) n=10 warm-pages + n=5 COLD-PAGES (drop_caches, disclosed) per product; L2 compare.cold_start + compare.warm_start (TUI launch_to_ready / first_paint / input_ready_gap) n=10 per product - the same harness drivers as the cmp5 corpus (the attach-paint lane's driver-shape family); L3 compare.memory_idle_load (10MiB fixture loaded, 3s settle, tree RSS+PSS) n=5 per product; L4 the TUI idle wake probe (2x180s windows, per-thread ctxt-switch attribution, keystroke latency after); L5 the parked-children census + headless baseline (parked_census.py): boot daemon with the offline mock, create parent, spawn K RLM children through the parent's kernel (rlm.spawn, each child runs an ipython cell - kernel boots, marker set - then settles), census+wake windows at settle / +150s / detach-the-owner-client then +360s, revival probes (child then parent); roles interleaved R,T,T,R at k=8 plus a k=0 headless rust leg; idleEvictionMinutes=1 via settings.json in BOTH the agent dir (PRIME_AGENT_CODING_AGENT_DIR is the live config root under the harness env) and the default home layout - the product's own global daemon policy surface, SAME config both sides, disclosed. L6 the TS tier-2 detached probe (one session, one turn, client detached immediately, tree watched 300s). INSTRUMENT: /proc statm RSS + smaps_rollup PSS per process, ppid-attributed tree walk from the daemon pid, utime/stime + per-thread voluntary/nonvoluntary ctxt switches (endpoint-only window sampling), a sleep-600 noop control riding every window, raw wire responses logged. INSTRUMENT FINDING (disclosed): /proc/PID/status ctxt counters are the LEADER THREAD's only - the prior fleet wake floors (106.4->2.0/s, TUI ~183/s) were leader rates; this census records leader AND thread-sum rates (the thread-sum is the true per-process rate). DRIVER BUGS FOUND+FIXED DURING AUTHORING (the fixture-shape lesson): the mock queue match must be a LIST (pick() iterates a bare string's characters, so every queue matched every request), and the settings file must land in the agent dir (a home-path settings.json is invisible under the env override).
parity_notes: No product change: wire/API/session-replay/prompts/TUI-output surfaces untouched. The TS legs use the product's own settings surface (idleEvictionMinutes) and its official release binary, not a clock hack; the drop_caches cold-pages legs are disclosed VM-state manipulations on the bench VM only. The comparison runs are bench-harness drivers, not product code.

parked_children_census.parity_verdict: The TS idle-eviction tier exists in the official release and fires at tier 2 (detached, whole-worker, proven); tier-1 child passivation was not observed in the census shape. The Rust port has NO idle eviction of any kind: the idleEvictionMinutes setting parses (pa-core settings manager, IdleEviction::Minutes) but has NO consumer - verified in source (no get_idle_eviction caller outside settings) and behaviorally (residency flat 2/2 at k=8 with the same settings both sides). With N settled children the port holds N x 54.6MB (median, range 50.5-59.4) indefinitely vs the TS reference's passivate-to-catalog-rows policy - the park-design reopen arm's trigger (a) (>=50MB/child at settle in production-like shapes) FIRES with the measured bound; this census is the arm's trigger (d) (the TS-parity sweep), so the arm rides with: the measured holding cost (54.6MB/child), the reference policy (tier-2 eviction <=120s detached at 1min), the revival budget (resident 0.12-0.19s; relaunch-class bounded by the launch legs ~0.3-1s), and the sweep's marginal wake cost in the port (+1 wake per cadence on the daemon's 2.5-2.8/s floor vs TS's already-130/s event loop).

validity.notes: The wake instrument finding: /proc/PID/status ctxt counters are the leader thread's only; the prior fleet wake floors (worker 106.4->2.0/s, TUI ~183/s) were leader rates - this census records leader AND thread-sum rates and the record's comparisons state which. The parked census's owner-client detach window was 90s - too short to observe the TS tier-2 eviction in-tree (the dedicated detached probe proves it at <=120s). The TS reference is the official 0.9.6 release (what users run); the parity-frozen surface (TS main cd1f215) carries the tier source-verified - the sweep arms at supervisor startup, cadence max(60s, idle/3), cap 2 child passivations per round.

outcome: decompose-complete (honest characterization record; no product change, no PR - measurement-only lane per the brief; the record, the margin ranking, and the surfaced candidates are the deliverables)
decision: The idle re-baseline at 50e011b78 (pre-#2741): (1) IDLE MEMORY - the composite floor is ~52% below the last measured tree baseline (498-517 -> ~237MB RSS/~199MB PSS at 10MiB loaded; worker ~158MB): the pole is MET and the margin vs the TS reference (770-1118MB) HOLDS at 2.8-4.5x - the single-session shape CLOSES. (2) IDLE CPU/WAKE - headless the tree is 4.5-4.6 wakes/s and ~0.04% of a core: both poles MET, the shape CLOSES; the TUI-attached tree is 184-189 wakes/s (the TUI's own ~10ms-poll thread class) - the pole is NOT met there and the candidate is bounded (park -> ~20-30/s); rust is ~25x better than the TS reference on idle wakes. (3) LAUNCH-TO-READY - daemon.boot HOLDS a 2.5-3.3x margin vs the only other daemon; the TUI leg is THIN vs the corpus best (11% behind cold / 23% behind warm) with the residual isolated to the ~214ms input_ready_gap (the attach-paint lane's co-gate, confirmed at the tip). (4) THE IDLE-EVICTION PARITY GAP - the port has NO idle eviction (dead setting, no consumer; residency flat 2/2 at k=8) while the TS reference evicts detached within <=120s: the parked-child cost is 54.6MB/child (median) held forever - the park-design whole-worker passivation arm's trigger (a) FIRES and the arm RIDES this census (trigger (d)); its measured bounds: 54.6MB/child reclaimable, revival 0.12-0.19s resident / ~0.3-1s relaunch-class, sweep cost +1 wake per cadence. NEXT-LANE RANKING (by the reach guideline): the parked-children passivation arm (the measured production-shape idle-memory class), then the TUI wake thread (~99.4/s, the #2880 class), with the input_ready_gap owned by attach-paint. The wake-instrument finding (leader-only /proc counters) retroactively qualifies every prior fleet wake figure - future wake lanes must record thread-sum rates.
